title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Crestline Bank
next_steps: Maya to send updated pricing and reserved capacity options by 2027-03-15
Liam to schedule on-prem benchmarking window with Daniel for week of 2027-03-22
Maya to share SOC 2 and ISO27001 reports plus KMS integration guide
Customer to confirm target regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1) and monthly committed tokens by 2027-03-19
Priya to begin internal PO process and share procurement timelines by 2027-03-25
action_items: Maya: Send pricing + dedicated capacity proposal (due 2027-03-15)
Liam: Arrange benchmark & provide test harness (due 2027-03-22)
Sophie: Share latency targets and internal compliance checklist (due 2027-03-18)
Priya: Prepare initial contract amendment draft and internal review notes (due 2027-03-25)
summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in. Crestline is evaluating a capacity upgrade to Redwood Dedicated across two regions, wants an on-prem benchmark for sensitive flows, and is asking for a one-year contract extension with committed tokens. Security and procurement items (SOC2, KMS, SSO) discussed; Redwood to provide pricing, docs, and benchmark plan.
meeting_header: Date: 2027-03-12 | Time: 15:00 - 15:42 PDT | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Sophie Ramirez (Crestline Head of AI), Daniel Kim (Crestline Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Crestline Procurement)
transcript:
00:00 - Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for making time today, this is the renewal and expansion check-in from Redwood, Maya here, and Liam from our solutions team is with me.
00:18 - Sophie: Hey Maya, thanks, yes we have about 40 minutes. We want to walk through capacity options and also the ask from procurement around the contract term.
00:35 - Liam: Great, quick agenda - status on current usage, options for Dedicated/reserved capacity, regions and on-prem options, security docs, and next steps. Sound ok?
00:50 - Daniel: Yep. Quick FYI our peak token rate has been up ~35% q/q, and the latency spikes more in the evenings. We hit a couple of timeouts last week on long-chat sessions.
01:08 - Maya: Thanks, that's helpful. On timeouts - do you recall if those were routed to our hosted API or to the dedicated cluster?
01:20 - Daniel: Hosted API, I think. The devs are using the hosted endpoint for staging. For production we have Dedicated but only a small pool.
01:32 - Sophie: Right, and as we expand more chat features we want predictable throughput. The team asked for a proposal to bump to 3x reserved GPUs and add eu-west-1.
01:47 - Liam: Ok, so two asks: scale capacity and add a region. We can do reserved capacity in increments, and we also have burst capacity for traffic spikes. For eu-west-1 we can replicate the Dedicated pool - there's a lead time to provision, usually 2-3 weeks depending on quota.
02:09 - Priya: From procurement side we also want to explore a one-year extension with committed tokens to get a better unit price. Can you share the pricing delta?
02:22 - Maya: Absolutely. I'll send a dedicated capacity tier sheet, showing per-GPU committed pricing and committed token discounts for 12- and 24-month terms. We'll include examples based on your current run rate + 50% uplift.
02:39 - Sophie: Perfect. Also, security - we need SOC2 and encryption at rest with our KMS. We might be looking at Private deployment for some PII flows; can Redwood run in our VPC?
02:55 - Liam: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages. We have a Private control plane option where you manage the networking and keys. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys - we have an HSM/KMS integration guide I can share.
03:14 - Daniel: Cool. For on-prem benchmarking, we need to run the exact model variant we use in prod; can you provide a test harness that simulates our sequence lengths?
03:28 - Liam: Yes, we'll provide a benchmark harness and a script that replays representative traces. We'll also surface KV cache hit rates and batching configs. That'll help tune quantization and batching to hit your latency targets.
03:45 - Sophie: On latency, we target p95 under 220ms for short prompts and under 800ms for streaming outputs. Is that realistic with Dedicated?
03:58 - Liam: It is, generally. Depends on sequence length distribution and whether you enable prefix caching. With proper batching and a 3x pool, p95 should be within your target for short prompts. For long streaming outputs you'll want to tune streaming chunk sizes and possibly use a higher-service tier or local region.
04:20 - Maya: Quick question on compliance - Sophie, do you need our SOC2 report or the full ISO artifacts?
04:30 - Sophie: SOC2 Type II is mandatory; ISO is helpful but optional. We also want RBAC for console access and audit logs sent to our SIEM.
04:41 - Liam: We have token-level logs and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console; audit log export to S3 or syslog is supported. We'll include sample log formats.
04:55 - Priya: Any blockers on SSO / SAML? We need SCIM sync for user provisioning.
05:03 - Maya: We support SSO SAML + SCIM; I'll attach the SSO metadata and a quick setup guide.
05:12 - Sophie: Great. On the contract extension - we'd like a committed token band that covers embeddings and generation. Can you clarify how embeddings units are counted?
05:25 - Maya: Embeddings are billed per 1k vectors or per 1k tokens depending on model family; we'll clarify exact metric per model in the sheet. For committed bands we can do blended pricing across endpoints.
05:38 - Daniel: About region parity, can you guarantee fallbacks if eu-west-1 has capacity constraints? We need graceful degradation not errors.
05:50 - Liam: Yes, smart routing can failover to another compatible region or to a slightly lower-cost model variant. We also support automatic fallback policies in rollout configs.
06:05 - Sophie: Ok, procurement note - we need the amendment to include SLAs for Dedicated latency and an SLA credit table.
06:15 - Maya: We can include SLA language for uptime and latency tiers for Dedicated. I'll have legal attach the SLA appendix.
06:23 - Priya: For billing cycles we prefer monthly invoicing with net-45 terms. Is that doable?
06:30 - Maya: We support monthly invoicing; net-30 is the default but we can escalate to finance to consider net-45 for enterprise agreements. I'll flag that.
06:40 - Daniel: Liam, you mentioned quantization earlier - are there model-quality regressions we should expect if we push 4-bit quant? We've seen hallucinations in other runs.
06:52 - Liam: Good question. Lower-bit quantization can slightly affect quality on rare cases. Our Optimize recommendations include per-workload evals and a guardrail: we can keep a small percentage of requests routed to the FP16 variant to monitor regressions and do progressive rollout.
07:10 - Sophie: That sounds good. Could we get an eval run on our 200 prompt seed set?
07:17 - Liam: Yes, send the prompt set and we'll run an eval and return a diff report with rouge/bleu style metrics and fail cases.
07:27 - Maya: For the region add - if you confirm eu-west-1 by Friday, we can start provisioning and have capacity in about 2 weeks.
07:35 - Sophie: We'll confirm by 2027-03-19, yes.
07:40 - Priya: On the price delta, if we commit to a 12-month term with X tokens, what's the uplift discount?
07:48 - Maya: Typically 10-18% depending on committed volume and whether you commit to Dedicated GPUs. I'll include a matrix in the proposal.
07:59 - Daniel: About benchmarks - we need to measure tail latency under realistic traffic shapes, not just single-run. Can the harness do traffic replay?
08:09 - Liam: Yes, the harness supports replay and spike injection to validate autoscaling and burst behavior. It will also log the KV cache metrics, so you can see cache hit rate impacts.
08:23 - Sophie: Regarding data residency - some of our PII flows must stay in EU. If we process in eu-west-1, is there any cross-region replication of logs by default?
08:35 - Liam: No cross-region replication by default for Private deployments; for hosted we can configure log retention and residency. For Dedicated we'll ensure logs stay in the selected region and provide retention policy configs.
08:50 - Maya: I'll make sure the security pack highlights data residency options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
09:00 - Sophie: Any limits on model variants in Dedicated? We want to pin a specific model hash for stability.
09:10 - Liam: You can pin model versions; we also support canary rollouts between model hashes. The runtime supports multiple model variants in a pool but pinned deploys give the most stability.
09:23 - Priya: Procurement also needs indemnity and standard data processing addendum. We'll expect our legal to share redlines after you send the amendment.
09:34 - Maya: Noted. We'll include a standard DPA and legal will be ready to review redlines.
09:42 - Sophie: Ok, let's talk numbers - current Dedicated is single 8-GPU pool on us-east-1. We're proposing to increase to 3x of that in us-east and mirror a 1x in eu-west-1. Does that align with Redwood's recommendation?
09:58 - Liam: Yes, that's a reasonable start. With that you should see much more consistent p95 latency. We can also enable autoscale with min/max to reduce cost while preserving SLO.
10:12 - Daniel: About autoscale - how fast does it scale up on spikes? We had a spike that lasted ~10 minutes and autoscaling didn't kick before some requests queued.
10:23 - Liam: Our autoscaler is policy-driven; you can tune aggressiveness. For spikes of 10 minutes you can set a shorter cool-down and faster scale-up thresholds. Also burst capacity helps for short spikes without provisioning more reserved GPUs.
10:38 - Sophie: Can you send a recommended autoscale policy for our workload?
10:43 - Liam: Yes, we'll include a recommended policy with suggested thresholds and expected cost impact.
10:50 - Priya: On invoicing, if we commit to a year's worth of tokens, can we get a single annual invoice?
10:58 - Maya: Yes, we can bill annually for committed contracts. We'll surface both monthly and annual billing examples.
11:05 - Sophie: Any known migration steps if we move some flows to Private? Do we need to change SDKs?
11:13 - Liam: No SDK changes required; endpoints change and you might update credentials. For Private there is a small networking setup and cert exchange. We'll provide a runbook.
11:25 - Sophie: Good. Also curious about observability - can Trace correlation tie back to our internal traces?
11:33 - Liam: We have tracing hooks and headers you can propagate; Console exposes per-route traces and you can export trace data to Jaeger or your APM.
11:44 - Maya: Quick pause - any blockers preventing us from moving forward to a renewed PO?
11:52 - Priya: The blockers are final pricing, SOC2 docs, and a procurement timeline alignment - once those are in place we can start PO.
12:04 - Maya: Ok we'll prioritize those. Liam will lead the benchmark setup and I'll own pricing and contract.
12:12 - Sophie: Can you also include a fallback strategy in the runbook? If eu-west is unavailable, we want a documented fallback flow.
12:22 - Liam: Yes we'll include fallback configs and routing policy examples.
12:30 - Daniel: For the benchmark week, we need read-only test harness and a whitelist of IPs to allow.
12:37 - Liam: We'll provide IP ranges and ephemeral keys for the test run.
12:44 - Sophie: On the security docs, we need a list of sub-processors and where logs are stored.
12:52 - Maya: That will be in the security packet. I'll add the sub-processor list and sample retention policies.
13:00 - Priya: If we accept the 12-month committment, what's the SLA credit for missed latency targets?
13:09 - Maya: We'll include a standard SLA table; credits tier with % of monthly fee depending on outage or latency breach severity. Legal can adjust on redline.
13:20 - Sophie: One more technical: our data scientist team wants to run ablations and sometimes needs model snapshots; can we keep snapshots accessible?
13:30 - Liam: Yes, model snapshots and KV caches can be checkpointed and exported. For Private, you can manage snapshots fully. For Dedicated we provide snapshot exports on request.
13:43 - Sophie: Terrific. Ok, any other questions from Redwood?
13:48 - Maya: Not right now. We'll recap and send deliverables.
13:52 - Liam: Quick list - pricing sheet, reserved capacity proposal, benchmark harness, SOC2 docs, SSO/SCIM guide, and an SLA appendix. We'll aim to get that to you by 2027-03-15 for pricing and 2027-03-22 for the benchmark setup.
14:12 - Sophie: That timeline works.
14:16 - Priya: We'll start internal procurement conversations once we receive the proposal.
14:22 - Maya: One last note on cost optimization - our Optimize team can provide batching and quantization recommendations to reduce token cost; if you want we can include a preliminary recommendation in the proposal.
14:35 - Sophie: Yes please include that.
14:40 - Daniel: For the benchmark, we'll provide the 200-prompt seed set and the traffic profile.
14:47 - Liam: Great, send that over to me and I'll instrument the harness accordingly.
14:53 - Sophie: Any rough estimate on cost delta for 3x capacity + a second region? Ballpark?
15:03 - Maya: Ballpark is 2.6x the current monthly if fully provisioned, but with autoscale and burst you can lower the steady-state cost - the committed discount will reduce it significantly. We'll put exact scenarios in the sheet.
15:18 - Priya: Ok, we'll review.
15:22 - Sophie: Thanks, this was useful.
15:25 - Maya: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the materials.
15:30 - Liam: I'll set up the benchmark tickets and share access requirements.
15:35 - Sophie: We'll confirm region decision by 2027-03-19 and send the prompt seed set this week.
15:42 - Maya: Awesome, talk soon.
15:44 - [Call ends]

Note: Transcript includes typical transcription artifacts; speaker labels based on calendar invite but may not reflect every speaker precisely.
